subject: [PATCH] mm/page_alloc: let the bulk and folio allocators carry alloc_flags

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledges that there are issues arising from rebasing on recent patches (ALLOC_NOLOCK and NOBLOCK) and plans to address them in a separate series, pulling out the NOBLOCK patch ahead of time.
reviews.raw_body:
Sashiko pointed out some issues that arise from rebasing on the recent
ALLOC_NOLOCK work, and in a quick review I found a similar slow-path
fallback issue with the NOBLOCK patch separate of this patch.

Brendan, if you're alright with it, can I pull the NOBLOCK patch out
ahead into a 2-commit series and I'll add the small fixups?

~Gregory

2026-09-14.patch_summary: This patch allows the bulk and folio allocators to carry allocation flags, enabling callers to select allocator behavior such as an alternate zonelist. The change adds new entry points in page_alloc.h that take an explicit alloc_flags parameter, matching the existing __alloc_pages_noprof() function. This modification does not introduce any functional changes, as all current callers pass ALLOC_DEFAULT. The patch is a preparatory step to address potential conflicts with other ongoing work on allocation flags.

reviews.author: Lance Yang
reviews.summary: Reviewer Lance Yang noted that __alloc_pages_bulk_noprof() can bypass the alloc_nolock_allowed() check and reach critical sections without verifying if locking is allowed, potentially causing a lock ordering violation.
reviews.raw_body:
Yeah, but what if a caller passes ALLOC_NOLOCK in the future?

__alloc_pages_noprof() checks alloc_nolock_allowed() first, but
__alloc_pages_bulk_noprof() can enter its fast path without that check.

That fast path can reach _deferred_grow_zone() or pcp_spin_trylock().
Shouldn't we do the same check first?

Or am I missing something?

Cheers, Lance

reviews.author: Gregory Price (author)
reviews.summary: Author acknowledged a concern about the NOLOCK flag and is reworking the patch to address this issue, incorporating changes from the ALLOC_UNMAPPED series.
reviews.raw_body:
There is some concern around NOLOCK here yes, in fact sashiko picked
this issue up and I've been poking at it.

I've actually been reworking this patch and pulled in changes from the
ALLOC_UNMAPPED series to address this all at once.  I've been developing
a page allocator unit-testing harness to help validate some assumptions
before I post it.

~Gregory
